calls.head: Point-blank against perimeter
calls.body: On shot quality, St. Louis sits 4th of 32, at the point-blank end of the scale. Chicago is 24th, at the perimeter end.
calls.call: St. Louis’s shots are more dangerous on average than Chicago’s.
calls.cite: Style fingerprint · this season blended with last · 2 and 3 games this season
calls.happened: On how dangerous the average unblocked shot was, St. Louis had 1 goal per 16.7 shots and Chicago 1 goal per 25.3 shots. Coming in, St. Louis was at 1 goal per 14.9 shots and Chicago at 1 goal per 16.3 shots.
calls.usual: STL 1 goal per 14.9 shots · CHI 1 goal per 16.3 shots
calls.tonight: STL 1 goal per 16.7 shots · CHI 1 goal per 25.3 shots

calls.head: St. Louis hits; Chicago mostly doesn’t
calls.body: St. Louis ranks 16th of 32 for physicality, toward the bruising end; Chicago ranks 31st, toward the finesse end.
calls.call: St. Louis hits more than Chicago in the close stretches of the game.
calls.cite: Style fingerprint · this season blended with last · 2 and 3 games this season
calls.happened: On hit score in close games (arena-adjusted, 100 is league average), St. Louis had 132 and Chicago 82. Coming in, St. Louis was at 100 and Chicago at 76.

CHI.head: We had this close to even (42% for Chicago), and Chicago came through.

STL.head: We had this close to even (58% for St. Louis), and it went Chicago’s way.

surprises.head: Chicago was kept to the outside
surprises.body: Chicago needed 25.3 unblocked shots per expected goal at 5-on-5, against its usual 16.3 and a league average of 15.8. Over the last three seasons, a team strayed this far about once every 35 games.

surprises.head: Chicago won against the run of play
surprises.body: Replaying this game’s chances, St. Louis comes out ahead 70 times in 100. Chicago won anyway.
